title: Region runner orchestration for cross-region latency/$ benchmark suites
author: Rina Kobayashi
body: Summary: Adds a first-class orchestrator to run the benchmark suite consistently across multiple Redwood regions with a single command, enforcing identical config (workload distribution, concurrency, warmup), per-region rate limiting/guardrails, and deterministic artifact aggregation. Motivation: We need repeatable, comparable per-region results for the public “latency per dollar” report; prior runs were manually kicked off per region and drifted in config and pacing, which showed up as avoidable variance and occasional load spikes. What’s included: (1) New CLI `benchmark-lab region-runner` that iterates a region list and runs the existing suite with a normalized config snapshot. (2) Per-region token-bucket rate limiting (QPS + concurrent in-flight) with optional jittered start to avoid synchronized bursts across regions. (3) Result aggregation that writes one region-level JSON artifact per run plus a top-level `aggregate.json` (and optional CSV) with a stable column order and explicit units. (4) Run metadata stamped into every artifact: git SHA, runner version, region, start/end timestamps, config hash, instance type label, and pricing source tag. (5) Failure handling: region runs are isolated; a single region failure does not abort the full matrix unless `--fail-fast` is provided. Retries are bounded and recorded as separate attempts with attempt_index. (6) Safety switches: `--dry-run`, `--max-total-runtime-min`, and hard caps for default concurrency/QPS to avoid accidental production impact when pointed at live endpoints. Implementation notes: The runner wraps the existing suite entrypoint rather than duplicating scenario logic; we generate a canonical config object, compute a SHA256 over the normalized JSON, and pass it through to suite invocations. Rate limiting is implemented client-side with an async semaphore (concurrency) + token bucket (QPS) and a per-request deadline so hung requests don’t stall aggregation. Aggregation uses streaming reads of per-region outputs to avoid high memory usage for long runs. CLI examples: `benchmark-lab region-runner --regions us-east-1,eu-west-1,ap-northeast-1 --suite chat_baseline --out artifacts/2025-01-27 --qps 8 --concurrency 32` and `benchmark-lab region-runner --regions-file configs/regions.public.json --suite embeddings_baseline --csv`. Output: `artifacts/<run_id>/<region>/summary.json` + `artifacts/<run_id>/aggregate.json` (+ `aggregate.csv` when enabled). Backward compatibility: Existing `benchmark-lab suite-runner` usage remains unchanged; region-runner is additive. Follow-ups: Variance thresholds and automatic rerun triggers are tracked separately (ENG-2872 / PR-153).
commits: cli: add region-runner command scaffold + args parsing
runner: normalize suite config + config hash stamping
rate-limit: token bucket + semaphore + per-request timeout
orchestration: region iteration, jittered start, bounded retries
artifacts: write region summaries + aggregate.json/csv builder
tests: unit tests for config normalization + aggregation ordering
docs: update README with region-runner examples and safety notes
review_conversation: Claire Dubois (Jan 23): Can we guarantee the exact same concurrency/sequence distribution is used per region? In past runs we saw small drift from hand-edited configs. Also, please ensure region labels match the marketing naming (e.g., eu-west-1 vs “EU (Ireland)”). Rina Kobayashi (Jan 23): Yep — region-runner now takes a single canonical config object, normalizes it (sorted keys, default filling), computes a config_hash, and passes the same blob into each suite invocation. Region naming: artifacts store the raw region code; I added `display_name` mapping in the sample regions file, but kept raw codes as primary keys for joins. Neha Kapoor (Jan 24): Safety concern — default settings should be conservative. Also add a guard so we don’t run more than N regions in parallel by default. Rina Kobayashi (Jan 24): Updated defaults to qps=4, concurrency=16, max_parallel_regions=1 unless explicitly set. Added `--dry-run` and `--max-total-runtime-min`. Sean Gallagher (Jan 25): For SRE review: please add per-request deadlines and ensure failures are surfaced clearly in aggregate output (not just logs). Also jitter starts; we don’t want synchronized thundering herd across regions. Rina Kobayashi (Jan 25): Added `--request-timeout-ms` default 30000 and a region-level `status` plus `error_summary` fields in aggregate.json. Implemented jittered start (0–3s) per region by default. Jonas Weber (Jan 26): Aggregation schema: keep units explicit (ms, tokens/s, $/1M tokens) and make sure stable column ordering for CSV. Sana Farid (Jan 26): Make sure attempt_index is recorded for retries; later variance analysis depends on knowing which runs were retries. Rina Kobayashi (Jan 26): Done — schema_v2 includes explicit units in field names where appropriate and CSV header is deterministic. attempt_index + is_retry are now part of both region summary and aggregate outputs. Claire Dubois (Jan 27): One more thing: please ensure the config hash includes warmup/caching policy knobs; those materially change latency. Rina Kobayashi (Jan 27): Good catch — normalization now includes warmup tokens, warmup duration, cache policy flags, and batching mode. All included in config_hash. Approvals: Claire Dubois (Jan 27), Sean Gallagher (Jan 27), Neha Kapoor (Jan 28), Jonas Weber (Jan 28).
release_notes: Internal-only: Added `benchmark-lab region-runner` to orchestrate consistent cross-region benchmark runs with rate limiting and aggregated artifacts.
